passage: The phone rang while Balram was eating, an unknown number. “This is the bank's customer care. Your father's account will be locked within ten minutes unless you read out the code we just sent.” A message had indeed landed with six digits. Balram's fingers went cold; his father had gone to the fields with the passbook. He almost read it out. Then he whispered to himself, “Why ten minutes? Why would a bank rush me? The rush is what they want.” He said, “I'll call the branch,” and the line went dead. His mother Urmila put down the roti. “Who was that?” “Someone who wanted the code, Ma. Nobody real ever asks for it.” They wrote the number on a scrap to show his father that evening.

qa.q: How many minutes did the caller say the account had?
What was Balram feeling when the message with the code arrived?
qa.a: Fear: his fingers went cold and he almost read the code out.

qa.q: What else could Balram do next, and why?
qa.a: Tell his father and ring the bank on the number in the passbook, since only an official channel can confirm whether the account is safe.

qa.q: How does the call look to Urmila?
qa.a: Urmila hears only one side and sees her son shaken by an unknown caller asking for a code, so she may be relieved that he stopped.

grounding: A teen gets a call with a ten-minute threat about his father's account and treats the urgency itself as the warning sign.

passage:
Jamal was halfway through a chess game with Hiroshi at the kitchen table in Leicester when his phone rang. A man's voice, fast and official: “This is your bank's security team. Your father's account gets frozen in ten minutes. A security code has just come to your phone. Read it to me now.”
Jamal's heart hammered. Dad was at work; a frozen account meant rent, the shopping, everything. His thumb was already opening his messages.
Then he stopped. Why ten minutes? he thought. Why is he so loud? Why do I feel like I can't breathe? A real bank would call Dad, not me. The hurry isn't a reason. The hurry is the trick.
“I'm not sharing any code,” he said, and hung up.
Hiroshi stared. “Was that real?”
“If it was real, it'll still be real in an hour,” Jamal said, and texted his dad.

qa.q: How long did the caller say Jamal had before the account was frozen?
What was Jamal feeling when his thumb started opening messages?
qa.a: He was frightened and panicky, heart hammering, picturing his father's account frozen.

qa.q: What else could Jamal do right after hanging up?
qa.a: Tell his dad and let him call the bank on the number printed on his card, never a number the caller gives.

qa.q: How might Hiroshi see what happened at the table?
qa.a: Hiroshi, surprised, sees a calm decision that the hurry itself was the warning, and learns the one-hour test too.

grounding: Shows a teen noticing the urgency and fear in a call demanding a code, and treating that pressure as the sign of a scam.

passage:
The hostel common room was loud with a carrom match when Uday's phone buzzed with an unknown number. He stepped into the corridor.
“Sir, this is your father's bank. His account is being blocked in ten minutes due to verification failure. You will get an OTP. Just read it out and I will stop the block.”
Uday said nothing for a second, and the voice went sharper. “Nine minutes, sir. Hurry.”
He walked back into the room and said, loud enough for Elizabeth at the notice board to hear, “Why would a bank need me, in a hurry? Why is he counting down? When someone makes me panic like this, that's the part I should trust least.”
He cut the call. Elizabeth, the house prefect, came over. “Report it to the warden?”
“Yes. And I'm calling Papa now.”
Ten minutes later, Papa confirmed his account was fine.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth suggest after the call?
What does Uday saying his thoughts aloud suggest about how he was feeling?
qa.a: It suggests he felt a jolt of panic but steadied himself by naming the countdown out loud, turning the fear into a warning sign.

qa.q: What else could the hostel do so other students are ready for such calls?
qa.a: The warden could describe this script at the next house meeting, so everyone knows to hang up and call family.

qa.q: How might Papa feel hearing about this call?
qa.a: Papa would likely be relieved the account is fine and proud that Uday refused to share the code.

grounding: Shows a teen reasoning aloud that a caller's countdown and pressure to share an OTP are themselves the warning sign.
